exercise.title: E, A and D
exercise.why: E is Em with one finger added, so a new chord is often an old one with a small change: look for what stays before you look for what moves.

cells.text:
Press a chord box below to hear the chord. Fret Em, then add the one finger that turns it into E.
Take that finger off and put it back, with a strum each time, until you hear the chord change with it.

Press a chord box below to hear the chord. Fret A as shown and pick its strings one at a time, from the A string to the high e string. Then do the same with D, from the D string.
Both chords leave their lowest strings out, so start each strum on the string the chord is named after.

Press Play below to start the metronome. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play: strum down on every beat, two bars on each chord.
Use the second bar to look ahead at the next shape. If a change comes late, keep your strumming hand going and catch the next beat 1.
